goal: Lock the smallest Bora-specific immigration-practicality doctrine for serious-role analysis: keep Initial OPT, future STEM OPT employer support, and future sponsorship familiarity distinct; make current role-specific employer wording control the employer-policy assessment for the current opening without replacing legal immigration authority; make E-Verify and I-983 operational support separately visible; prohibit employer-size or historical-filing shortcuts; and keep doctrine status-neutral unless current Candidate Truth explicitly establishes a personal authorization fact.
acceptance_conditions: BLUEPRINT version and project_state latest_locked_section/version remain mechanically consistent
Initial OPT practicality, future STEM OPT employer support, and future sponsorship familiarity are explicitly separate in serious-role analysis
E-Verify evidence and I-983 employer willingness/support are explicitly distinct; E-Verify alone must not imply I-983 willingness
current role-specific work-authorization/sponsorship wording outranks employer historical H-1B/LCA familiarity for the current opening
no-sponsorship wording is not automatically converted into no-OPT eligibility; consequential legal ambiguity remains LEGAL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED or human/HR verification
company size, prestige, industry, recruiter enthusiasm, and historical filing absence remain non-determinative signals only
existing immigration source hierarchy and UNKNOWN/fail-closed semantics are preserved
python scripts/verify_assurance_baseline.py reports ALL PHASES PASSED
independent Cursor adversarial review returns SAFE
No unsupported population-wide claim such as most employers already satisfy E-Verify may remain
Current role-specific posting/HR wording controls employer-policy assessment for that opening but must not be presented as legal authority for OPT/STEM eligibility

stop_conditions: closing the doctrine would require a new immigration/legal determination not supported by USCIS, DHS/SEVP, E-Verify, Brandeis ISSO, or another approved authority
closing the doctrine would require a new schema field or enum, qualification/decision runtime change, automated legal conclusion, or employer-size scoring model
closing the doctrine would require modifying Candidate Truth, resume/package doctrine, job-discovery providers, or application submission logic
the change would collapse Initial OPT, STEM OPT, E-Verify, I-983 support, or future sponsorship into one state
the change would create numeric sponsorship/immigration probabilities or weights
